label: The refusal catalogue exists in code (REFUSAL_CAUSES, 25 entries with an author/operator/environment class) and no phase cites it, while 007-011 mint about 36 new names that must join it.
RefusalDetail.cause is typed string rather than RefusalCause, so the registry is not enforced at the record boundary.
No phase owns the exit-code convention: EXIT_CODES is a frozen six-value object and zero of 14 phase specs cite it, each restating a bare number instead.

The packet has no schema-version concept: no state-root marker and no record version field, while five phases edit closed-key lists and the only compatibility rule is read a missing field as a default.
Migration and rollback are mentioned about ten times across fourteen phases and owned by none; no phase has a migration section, rollback step or operator upgrade runbook.
Concurrency is handled per phase but never as one rule: queue owners state their rules in detail and shared-file writers such as 008 index state none, with no packet-level single-writer map.
No phase states which of its refusals are pre-dispatch and which are post-dispatch, so a builder cannot tell whether to write RunExit.refusal or RunExit.reason.
Refusal names are minted across three document layers with no single list, so a name can be prose-only and absent from the REQ table and the acceptance criteria.
